name: mimem
description: Turn a paper into audio designed to be remembered: questions, spacing, and nothing invented.
long_description:
mimem rewrites a document so that the text itself does what a careful reader would have done — because listening removes every one of those moves and a speech engine puts nothing back.

Give it a PDF, an EPUB, a link or pasted text and it builds a **programme**: an orientation, a few questions to hold on to, the terms defined before they are used, the paper in segments that each end on a question with a pause long enough to actually try, and the ideas that matter coming back at growing intervals.

**Nothing is invented.** Every sentence is either the paper's own — carrying the exact place it came from — or one of about a dozen named templates. When you write the explanations, every number in what you write is checked against the sentences it was written from, and a claim that reverses the paper's direction is rejected before it reaches the programme. You watch that happen.

**No API key.** The explanations are written in the conversation, by the assistant you are already talking to.

Also: study sessions. Ask what is due and it quizzes you on the cards from every programme you have built, scheduled across days.

workspace.title: Where programmes are written
workspace.description: One directory, so nothing is ever scattered. Defaults to a 'mimem' folder in your home directory.

listener_file.title: What you already know
listener_file.description: Optional path to a listener.yaml listing terms you do not need explained. Without it, mimem assumes you are new to the field and defines more.

default_profile.title: Default profile
default_profile.description: skim, study or drill. 'study' is the sensible default: full length, a question at the end of every segment.

tools.description: What the programme would like explained: glosses, concrete anchors, analogies.

tools.name: apply_elaborations
tools.description: Store explanations you wrote, after checking every number against the source.

tools.name: study_session
tools.description: The cards due for review, across every programme.

tools.name: grade_card
tools.description: Record whether a card was recalled, and schedule the next review.

tools.name: review_status

tools.name: explain_beat

tools.name: set_concept
tools.description: Correct a concept's ranking or its definition, permanently.
